As mods's incentives will come under SCU* (Solo Contributors' Union) from next month, proposing a SuperMajority referendum for their March month's incentives (Treasury Proposal #59). 
7-Day Trailing Average: $ 0.0058 per EDG
Thus, 2000 USD equivalent amount = 344827.586 EDG
Incentives per moderator = 86206.8965 EDG

*{dedicated framework draft coming soon.}

The bounty process is quite lengthy and is not fine-tuned as compared to other governance parameters.
So for the 2000 USD equivalent monthly incentives ($500*4) for the community mods in Feb 2022, I am proposing a treasury tip.
7-Day Trailing Average: $ 0.004 per EDG
Thus, 2000 USD equivalent amount = 500000 EDG
Incentives per moderator = 125000 EDG

The bounty (#3) for 2000 USD equivalent monthly incentives ($500*4) for the community mods is now live for voting.
7-Day Trailing Average: $ 0.0049 per EDG
Thus, 2000 USD equivalent amount = 408163.265 EDG
So does this bounty go through the series of steps and then to simplemajority referendum ?
No, the bounty process doesn't have a referendum stage,

New upcoming moderator are already helping the new comers 
Thank you to them

When I took the quiz, I was working in the background and I had no idea that it's part of the Moderators' Recruitment. I would have prepared for that if only I knew :)

And, I think it would be a good idea to gather information from potential moderators about their living location(APAC/EMEA/AMER), about working/studying situation and general availability, as maybe some people are working in shifts or are available in certain hours. All this information should be taken into account before making the final decisions.

The quiz was announced everywhere (Twitter, TG, Reddit). Curious to know if you have any suggestions on how we can deliver updates to everyone more effectively. 
Thanks for the great feedback on the timezone allocation. If a certain timeframe is not suitable for any of the 4 selected mods, we could onboard 5th one without the removal of already selected ones.

2 quiz participants reported that many TG accounts joined just before the quiz and left the group after the quiz highlighting the possibility of manipulation using multiple accounts for the questions with fewer options.
Thus I proposed a solution of hosting another quiz between top 10 ranking quiz participants in a private group (with Edgeware contributors for transparency).
Here is more info on that: [https://t.me/heyedgeware/65988](https://t.me/heyedgeware/65988)

Thanks, [@Vismay Joshi](/edgeware/account/mNh7aSGrMcVWXNEic8VDpoLTe1SWmhNa9eaC1umV3E4u3pm) and [@Sarvesh](/edgeware/account/jZJBw4gWvb9DE5yCu51v7ojUkkmRQdYkK4aneJX89dL3Ep8) for great counter-points on TG and here. I expect feedback on the topic from other quiz participants and Edgeware contributors. Also opening up a poll here for the community to decide the optimal solution/path.

To,
The head of community,
As in the above information provided, it is written that the 4 winner moderators are going to be on a 1 month trial. So basically if anyone doesn't perform well they are not going to move forward. And then again the already winners are risking their jobs. Also I just want to give my personal opinion that is, you should take a poll that there must be  another quiz or not. And I think even if there will be minimum 2 votes for 'No' then it must count. Because we are going to be on trial period as written. This satisfies decentralization according to me.

To whom it may concern:
      I Carlos, would be honored to continue to serve as moderator/spam eliminator on the behalf of the edgeverse community. Edgeware has become a home to me on the meta/online world, and I wouldn't change it. I am here for the long haul, trying to learn as much as I can when I can. Life keeps me plenty busy.
On a side note I am very active on twitter and will keep bringing Edgeware news and info to those who are not in the know and make sure our voice is heard. 
Even a whisper can sound like a trumpet.
